body: Why is this controlled via a project setting? It seems very odd to me to enforce a single line width for every line in the project.

> Why is this controlled via a project setting? It seems very odd to me to enforce a single line width for every line in the project. 

Calinou wanted to have an editor setting in addition to the project setting in his original PR, would we want to include that, or just specify 1 editor setting for everything?

> > Why is this controlled via a project setting? It seems very odd to me to enforce a single line width for every line in the project.
> 
> Calinou wanted to have an editor setting in addition to the project setting in his original PR, would we want to include that, or just specify 1 editor setting for everything?

What is the justification for either? The original proposal is asking for wider lines for editor AABB drawing. I think it is worth stepping back and asking yourself "how does this PR solve that users need?" The user wants the AABB's in the editor to be more visible. They suggest allowing the Gizmo line width to be configurable. But our job here is to ensure that the user's need is met, not that we implement a feature in the way a user requests it. 

With this approach the user would need to configure the line width manually for each project they have, which will be a pain. It also isn't available on MacOs, iOS, Web, Android, or Windows + D3D12, or any project using the compatibility renderer.

These trade offs were made because this is the simplest way to add configurable line widths. But configurable line widths aren't what the user _needs_ it is just what they asked for because they didn't understand the complexity behind variable line width in modern graphics APIs and it seemed like an easy request.

You know that is a great way to put it. I think as a baseline, having the line width being customizable is a good thing, because even besides AABBs, the Grid and Collison lines seen in my screenshot are much more visible (especially on a higher resolution monitor), but like you and @Calinou said, this way seems too much like a bandaid at this point. 

The way Calinou described "-we'll want an universal way to emulate thick line drawing using screen-aligned quads", seems to be the way to go.

(_Even_ researching into D3D12 to see if there's a way to change line width comes up with nothing, not sure if that's true or not but man anything graphics related is **hard** lol).

I'll keep this open incase anyone wants to cherry-pick into their fork.

We could avoid having either a project or dedicated editor setting by reading the editor scale setting, and multiplying the line width by the editor scale automatically. This way, lines will appear to have the same physical size on a hiDPI display than they would do on a lowDPI display at a lower resolution.

This may not suffice for all use cases (users with low vision might find the lines still not thick enough), but it's a good start.

That could work and would be nice and easy. 

What still gets me (and forgive my god awful knowledge of graphics APIs) but from _above_, it looks like were looking at:

**<ins>Unsupported:</ins>**
- Metal

**<ins>Supported:</ins>**
- Vulkan
- Compatibility (w/ [glLineWidth](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/glLineWidth.xhtml))?

**<ins>?:</ins>**
- D3D12 (couldn't find anything on how this could be done)

So at what point do we ignore a solution like this and worry about the one that would cover all of these?

> So at what point do we ignore a solution like this and worry about the one that would cover all of these?

To get back to this PR, the issue is that macOS is arguably the platform with the highest percentage of hiDPI users (given Retina displays are on nearly all Apple products now). It's also a platform that does not support thick lines in hardware, so a different solution is needed. This also applies to iOS where it can be an issue for ports of the Godot editor there, such as Xogot.

This is why we should look into implementing screen-aligned quads instead (and using them when the line thickness is different from `1.0`). It's significantly more complex, but I'm sure it'll be worth the effort. On top of that, https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5196 would also benefit from having a screen-aligned quad line drawing solution.
